message.content:
Here are a few of the most popular and highly regarded sushi spots in Tokyo:

| Restaurant | Highlights | Location |
|------------|------------|----------|
| **Sukiyabashi Jiro** | Legendary chef Jiro Ono; Michelin‑starred, famed for precision and quality. | Ginza (Tokyo Station area) |
| **Sushi Saito** | Intimate 10‑seat setting; Michelin‑starred; known for impeccable nigiri and service. | Minato Ward |
| **Sushi Yoshitake** | Michelin‑starred; offers a refined omakase experience with seasonal ingredients. | Chiyoda Ward |
| **Sushi Dai** | Located at Tsukiji Outer Market; renowned for fresh fish and long lines. | Tsukiji |
| **Sushi Iwa** | Small, intimate setting; Michelin‑starred; focuses on traditional Edomae style. | Chuo Ward |
| **Sushi Masuda** | Known for its “sushi bar” concept and high-quality fish. | Shinjuku |
| **Sushi Mizutani** | Michelin‑starred; offers a modern take on classic sushi. | Chiyoda Ward |
| **Sushi Kyubey** | Classic Tokyo sushi chain; offers both casual and premium options. | Ginza & other locations |
| **Sushi Sawada** | Michelin‑starred; known for its creative presentations and seasonal menu. | Chiyoda Ward |
| **Sushi Tsubaki** | Michelin‑starred; offers a quiet, refined dining experience. | Chiyoda Ward |

These restaurants range from high‑end Michelin‑starred establishments to more accessible market stalls. If you’re planning a visit, it’s wise to make reservations well in advance—especially for the Michelin‑starred spots, which often have limited seating and require booking months ahead. Enjoy your sushi adventure!
